summary: @servicetitan/folder-lint preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package advertises itself as a folder-lint schema (glob/minimatch types) but ships a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that fires automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs — itself obfuscator.io-style with hex-encoded identifiers — downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (dl("https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v"+V+...)), extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync(bunBinary, [path.join(D,"math_init.js")], {stdio:"inherit", cwd:D}). math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript file (rotating string-array decoder WV8StW over a large mixed constant array n7gIxM, randomized hex-style identifiers, `// @bun @bun-cjs` tag) whose name and content are unrelated to the declared folder-lint schema purpose. The alternate runtime is used specifically to execute code that Node-based install-time scanners would not run, and the payload's real behavior is not readable without executing the decoder. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: attacker-controlled obfuscated code runs with the installer's privileges on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
